newsitem.title: USA: Rank seen putting up $50 mln for Castle redo.
newsitem.headline: Rank seen putting up $50 mln for Castle redo.

text.p: Rank Organisation Plc is expected to roll into the U.S. gaming market with a $50 million outlay to renovate Atlantic City's Trump Castle as a Hard Rock Cafe & Casino, sources close to the situation said.
Rank is negotiating with Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc to reflag the Castle as a Hard Rock, and a deal could be announced as early as next week, the sources said.

The agreement would mark Rank's debut in the $17 billion U.S. casino gaming industry and is expected to precede a possible 50 percent acquisition of the Castle from Trump Hotels for $150 million and assumption of one-half of the property's $350 million debt, the sources said.

Trump Hotels chairman Donald Trump "clearly wants to do something and do it yesterday," a source said. "He wants to get the whole marina renovation going and Rank is saying, 'Wait for us.' But Trump does not want to wait because he wants to establish market position before Steve Wynn gets to town." Wynn is chairman of Mirage.

"Right now, I don't know if Rank is ready yet to write a check for $150 million, but their end game is being a major player in the U.S. gaming market. They own the Hard Rock name and spent a lot of money to get it. They have to leverage that investment and this is a great way to do it," he added.

The Castle and Harrah's Entertainment Inc's casino now are the only gaming properties in Atlantic City's marina, a duopoly expected to end with Mirage Resorts Inc $500 million development of the nearby 178-acre "H" Tract.
A Trump spokesman referred all calls to Hard Rock headquarters in Orlando, Fla., where president Jim Berk was not available to comment.
Officials at Rank's London headquarters were not immediately available to comment.

The sources said Rank's intends to learn the business before undergoing the onerous and lengthy New Jersey gaming licensing process, generally required when a party holds five percent of the equity in a casino operator.

"The deal structure may not be what Rank's end game is. Retheming the Castle would be a $50 million investment and a first step in a series of transactions. After they got license, got comfortable with the market, I absolutely see them buying an Atlantic City property," said the first source.

"As far as a direct investment in the Trump parent company, that would trigger a licensing issue. Re-theming is a nonlicensable event, and Rank will consider what further role they want to play" after the Castle renovation, said a second source.
The sources agreed that part of the talks centered around how the high-value, franchise names "Trump" and "Hard Rock" will be applied in the joint venture.
"There was a big issue with the names, and it now looks like it will be called the Hard Rock at Trump's Marina," a third source said.
Meanwhile, Rank executives were in the United States about three weeks ago shopping for a U.S.-based investment bank to guide it through the gaming landscape, the sources said.
Rank visited the three Wall Street firms with established gaming groups -- Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, Bear Stearns and Salomon Bros -- but has yet to make a formal hiring, they said.

In June, Rank paid Peter Morton $410 million for the chain he founded 25 years ago in London, a deal that added 13 Hard Rock Cafes and four franchises to the 15 cafes and 26 franchises already held by Rank.

Morton retained the right to develop the brand in the United States west of the Mississippi River, and his Hard Rock Hotel and Casino opened last year quickly became one of the city's most successful operations.

"Everyone though the Hard Rock in Las Vegas was going to bomb. They said it had a bad location near the airport, off the "Strip." But it's a home run, the hottest property in Las Vegas," the first source said.
